item.title: Pope Leo XIV ends his visit to Uruguay with a tribute to women before departing to Argentina
item.description: Tens of thousands of people packed Florida’s main square for the Mass under brilliant blue skies, some walking for several kilometers to reach the site. The city has a population of about 40,000 but the Vatican estimated 50,000 were attending.

item.title: Overcrowded car plunges into lake in Brazil, killing ten, including five children
item.description: The Rio de Janeiro government confirmed ten dead, including five children. Brazilian media say a baby was among the victims.

item.title: Erdoğan joins Aliyev for Azerbaijan’s Victory Day in Karabakh
item.description: Azerbaijan celebrated on Sunday its sixth Victory Day, marking the end of the Karabakh war. Turkey's Erdoğan joined the commemorations to underscore the strength of bilateral ties despite recent differences, with Aliyev declaring that "this unity will last forever".

item.title: Rosstat hack: data obtained suggests over 390,000 Russian deaths in Ukraine war
item.description: Hacker groups Cyberpartisans BY and Silent Crow say they hacked Rosstat and counted Russian losses since the invasion of Ukraine. Their tally: between 393,000 and 450,000 killed.

item.title: Watch: Spectacular double waterspout forms off Italy's Capri island
item.description: A rare double waterspout formed over Capri's iconic Faraglioni rock formations on Saturday, as heavy clouds gathered above the Italian island.

item.title: At least seven dead, more than 100 injured as two trains collide south of Cairo
item.description: The accident occurred about 52 kilometres south of Cairo, when one train hit the rear of another and one derailed. Egyptian President Abdelfatah al-Sisi has ordered an investigation to determine the causes and responsibility.

item.title: More than 200 tarantula sightings in Austria in two months
item.description: Tarantulas are particularly active in the autumn, when they search for sheltered spots to spend the winter.

item.title: UK pays tribute to armed services members fallen in conflicts on Remembrance Sunday
item.description: Remembrance Sunday is held on the second Sunday in November, nearest to Armistice Day on 11 November, the anniversary of the end of World War I, and is led by the monarch.

item.title: Russian strikes on Ukraine leave 850,000 without power as Zelenskyy reports drone attack on Komyshuvakha
item.description: Zelenskyy said Russia had launched a drone strike on the site of a recent attack on Komyshuvakha, where rescuers have been carrying out search operations following a bombing that killed at least 55 people on Monday.

item.title: Europeans to join Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, says French FM Barrot
item.description: "No one will speak in our name", French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot says, adding that Europeans will join next week's Russia-Ukraine talks. He also accused hard left presidential candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon of echoing Kremlin propaganda.

item.title: Egypt reopens Tripoli embassy after 12 years and raises concerns over Turkey-Libya maritime deal
item.description: Egypt is seeking closer ties with Libya’s western government after years of backing its eastern rival. Talks in Tripoli covered energy projects and Egypt’s objections to Libya’s maritime deal with Turkey.

item.title: Condolences and solidarity: European and world leaders react to Krakow shooting.
item.description: The tragedy in Krakow sparked reactions worldwide. Leaders of Germany, France, Italy, Ukraine, the Baltic states, the EU and the US offered condolences, stressing: "Poland does not stand alone".

item.title: Egypt announces new Mediterranean gas field discovery estimated at 200 billion cubic feet
item.description: The Ministry of Petroleum attributed the positive results to higher investment and exploration activity, noting a better investment climate and progress in settling overdue payments to foreign companies in the energy sector.

item.title: US forces strike commercial vessel in Gulf of Oman after crew 'ignored repeated warnings'
item.description: The UKMTO maritime agency said late on Saturday that it had received a report of an incident involving a bulk carrier and military forces in the gulf.

item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 8th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Canary Islands demand urgent government action amid surge in migrant arrivals
item.description: Between 1 and 6 November, 49 boats carrying a total of 4,587 migrants arrived in the Canary Islands, according to the regional government.

item.title: At least 21 dead after migrant boat capsizes off Senegal, authorities say
item.description: The United Nations' International Organization for Migration (IOM) says the dangerous Atlantic Route is a key pathway for West African migrants travelling to Europe.

item.title: Grand Prix d’Horlogerie de Genève 2026: Rexhep Rexhepi wins prestigious Aiguille d’Or Prize
item.description: At this year's luxury watch awards, 84 timepieces and clocks were in competition across 14 categories, including sports, calendar and astronomy, jewellery and mechanical exception.

item.title: Netanyahu rival Eisenkot to be tasked with forming new government following Israeli elections
item.description: In Israel, a candidate tasked with forming a new government has 28 days to carry out the job. The president is able to extend this by a maximum of 14 days before giving the mandate to someone else.

item.title: What we know about the Krakow shooting that left six people dead
item.description: Police said the bodies of the suspect's 53-year-old father, 52-year-old mother and 21-year-old sister had also been found at his home.

item.title: Fjord Oslo: Norway’s capital celebrates peace at open-air light art festival
item.description: The Norwegian capital is hosting the fifth edition of Fjord Oslo, an international festival showcasing outdoor light art. This year's edition brings together artists from several countries to explore the meaning of peace through installations across the city.

item.title: Trump offers UFC boss White House press secretary role: 'Dana, please take the job!'
item.description: Trump and White have forged a close relationship over the years, with Trump a regular attendee at UFC events and White having spoken at a number of the president's rallies.

item.title: Where would you go in a time machine? Physicist says time travel only goes forward
item.description: Pack for tomorrow, not yesterday. A physicist says time travel to the past could be impossible.

item.title: ‘We’re hardly producing any power’: Can Europe’s solar boom survive a cloudy winter?
item.description: A prolonged period of cloudy and windless weather can throttle Europe's solar and wind generations, often causing the grid to rely on polluting back-up sources.

item.title: Cheek kisses, shoes off and punctuality: European social etiquette rules travellers should know
item.description: From taking your shoes off indoors to being on time, a new survey reveals the social etiquette rules that travellers should know before heading to Europe.

item.title: Poland: Footage shows people taking cover as a gunman opens fire in Krakow
item.description: Footage shows people fleeing as cars speed away during a deadly shooting at Krakow's Main Market Square, which left six people dead and about 15 injured.

item.title: Ukraine: Russian strikes hit Kyiv region, damaging infrastructure
item.description: Russian strikes have damaged infrastructure in the Kyiv region and left a kindergarten in ruins in the Ukrainian capital. Firefighters battled a major blaze as Ukraine faced renewed attacks on its energy network.

item.title: Liverpool FC targets counterfeit pro-Palestinian shirts using altered club crest
item.description: On the internet, fake Premier League shirts with pro-Palestinian slogans are on sale, affecting, among other clubs, Liverpool F.C. The Reds are now taking action.

item.title: Video shows people fleeing as gunman opens fire in Kraków, Poland
item.description: UGC footage shows people running for cover as a deadly shooting unfolds in Kraków, Poland, leaving at least six people dead and around a dozen wounded, according to police.

item.title: 'Peace is possible and we are called to build it' Pope Leo XIV says in Uruguay
item.description: The Pontiff was welcomed by 40,000 people in Paysandú, Uruguay. Leo's sixth apostolic journey comes less than a month after lung adenocarcinoma surgery at Rome's Gemelli Hospital.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 7th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 7th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: ‘We need to change everything’: Mélenchon uses Le Bourget rally to press home his programme
item.description: The right to vote at 16, a Sixth Republic as a “new ecological state”: the four-time Élysée candidate outlined his presidential programme to more than 20,000 supporters. A further show of strength against a backdrop of social unrest in the country.

item.title: Six killed and more than a dozen injured after gunman opens fire in historic centre of Kraków
item.description: The suspect, a 25-year-old Polish citizen, was fascinated with far-right ideologies and held “very radical" and “ultra-nationalistic" views, Polish Interior Minister Marcin Kierwiński said.

item.title: Russia fires North Korean missiles at 'key' Ukrainian energy facility, Zelenskyy says
item.description: "Moscow is deliberately seeking to leave millions of Ukrainians without electricity, heating, and water as winter approaches," Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said.

item.title: Spain: Baby's body found in freezer in Ourense may have been there over 20 years
item.description: The body of the newborn was discovered in a chest freezer in a storage room in Allariz (Ourense) and may have been there for over 20 years, according to local newspaper 'La Región'.

item.title: Cyberattacks target Italian foreign minister and company behind Brenner Base Tunnel project
item.description: The company behind the under-construction Brenner Base Tunnel project - a 55 km rail link between Innsbruck in Austria and Fortezza in Italy - confirmed it had also been hit by a cyberattack in recent weeks.

item.title: US launches new targeted strikes on Iran as Trump claims progress in talks with Tehran
item.description: The US military carried out new airstrikes on Iranian defence systems, sending ripples across the Gulf, but Trump insists they are “minor strikes” while intense diplomatic efforts continue to avert an all-out war.

item.title: US offers $20 million reward and 'possible relocation' for information on 'Iran’s nuclear program'
item.description: The State Department said: "The regime’s lack of compliance with the IAEA on safeguards obligations has led to the agency’s loss of 'continuity of knowledge.'"

item.title: Pedro Alliana sworn in as Paraguay president after Santiago Peña's impeachment
item.description: Ousted ex-President Santiago Peña was placed under house arrest on Friday after he was impeached over a major banking crisis.

item.title: US Secret Service arrests man parked near White House with 'multiple guns' in vehicle
item.description: The suspect has been charged with multiple offences, including possession of dangerous weapons and theft, per the DHS. He is in the custody of the US Marshals Service.

item.title: New Zealand counts votes in razor-thin election after campaign centred on cost of living
item.description: In New Zealand, people cast a party vote as well as an electorate vote in a general election. With their electorate vote, New Zealanders vote for a candidate to represent their local electorate in parliament. They also vote for the party they want to be in government.

item.title: Hackers probed Europe’s fridge systems weeks before cyberattacks. Who did it and what could they target next?
item.description: The attacks exposed basic security weaknesses in connected refrigeration systems, but experts warn that similar vulnerabilities could put everything from supermarket equipment to hospital and data centre infrastructure at risk.

item.title: When antibiotics stop working: Europe's growing superbug threat
item.description: Antimicrobial resistance, responsible for an estimated 35,000 deaths each year in the European Union, is spreading across humans, animals and the environment, prompting calls for a broader approach to tackling one of public health's biggest challenges.

item.title: Russian strikes on Kyiv region injure at least six and damage bridge and energy facilities
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned on Friday night of further strikes against Ukraine's energy sector and civilian infrastructure as he renewed calls for deliveries of Patriot interceptor missiles.

item.title: Europe needs Cold War-like deterrence for AI warfare, Poland says
item.description: The rise in AI-powered cyberattacks requires Europe to build a deterrence system similar to the one that prevented mutual destruction during the Cold War, Polish Deputy Minister Krzysztof Gawkowski has said.

item.title: ‘Brief burst of intense heat’ could give hard-to-recycle wind turbine blades a second life
item.description: Europe risks becoming a dumping ground for hard-to-recycle wind turbine blades but new research has found a ‘hot’ solution

item.title: Earn points, save cash: A basic guide to frequent-flyer programmes in Europe
item.description: With airline alliances and partnerships, frequent flyers can rack up miles in their sleep.
